claim: Patient-drug treatment matching fails in a subset of AML patients harboring atypical internal tandem duplications (ITDs) in the tyrosine kinase domain of the FLT3 gene.
source: In the setting of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), patient-drug treatment matching fails in a subset of patients harboring atypical internal tandem duplications (ITDs) in the tyrosine kinase domain of the FLT3 gene.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a motivation for the study, representing the clinical problem being addressed.

claim: FLT3-ITD is one of the most common driver mutations in AML.
source: FLT3-ITD, one of the most common driver mutations in AML, occurs in exons 15 and 16, which encode the juxtamembrane domain (JMD) and the first tyrosine kinase (TKD1) domain, and results in constitutive activation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Introduction section.

claim: FLT3-ITD occurs in exons 15 and 16, which encode the juxtamembrane domain (JMD) and the first tyrosine kinase (TKD1) domain.
source: FLT3-ITD, one of the most common driver mutations in AML, occurs in exons 15 and 16, which encode the juxtamembrane domain (JMD) and the first tyrosine kinase (TKD1) domain, and results in constitutive activation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the molecular location of FLT3-ITD mutations.

claim: FLT3-ITD results in constitutive activation of the FLT3 receptor.
source: FLT3-ITD, one of the most common driver mutations in AML, occurs in exons 15 and 16, which encode the juxtamembrane domain (JMD) and the first tyrosine kinase (TKD1) domain, and results in constitutive activation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the functional consequence of FLT3-ITD mutations.

claim: The location (insertion site) of the ITD is a crucial prognostic factor in FLT3-ITD AML.
source: We and others have demonstrated that the location (insertion site) of the ITD is a crucial prognostic factor: treatment with the recently FDA-approved multi-kinase inhibitor Midostaurin and standard frontline chemotherapy has a significant beneficial effect only in patients carrying the ITDs in the JMD domain, whereas no beneficial effect has been shown in patients carrying ITDs in the TKD region (Rücker et al., 2022; Pugliese et al., 2023; Massacci et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work by the authors and others.

claim: Treatment with Midostaurin and standard frontline chemotherapy has a significant beneficial effect only in patients carrying ITDs in the JMD domain.
source: We and others have demonstrated that the location (insertion site) of the ITD is a crucial prognostic factor: treatment with the recently FDA-approved multi-kinase inhibitor Midostaurin and standard frontline chemotherapy has a significant beneficial effect only in patients carrying the ITDs in the JMD domain, whereas no beneficial effect has been shown in patients carrying ITDs in the TKD region (Rücker et al., 2022; Pugliese et al., 2023; Massacci et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: No beneficial effect of Midostaurin treatment has been shown in patients carrying ITDs in the TKD region.
source: We and others have demonstrated that the location (insertion site) of the ITD is a crucial prognostic factor: treatment with the recently FDA-approved multi-kinase inhibitor Midostaurin and standard frontline chemotherapy has a significant beneficial effect only in patients carrying the ITDs in the JMD domain, whereas no beneficial effect has been shown in patients carrying ITDs in the TKD region (Rücker et al., 2022; Pugliese et al., 2023; Massacci et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Differences underlying tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) sensitivity are related to a genotype-specific rewiring of the involved signaling networks.
source: Moreover, our group and others have demonstrated that the differences underlying tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) sensitivity are related to a genotype-specific rewiring of the involved signaling networks.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work by the authors and others.

claim: JNK plays a crucial role in the TKI response of FLT3-ITD cells through a cell cycle-dependent mechanism.
source: These models revealed that JNK plays a crucial role in the TKI response of FLT3-ITD cells through a cell cycle-dependent mechanism, in line with our previous findings (Massacci et al., 2023; Pugliese et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the current study, supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The FLT3-ITD PKN included 76 nodes and 193 edges.
source: The so-obtained pre-PKN included 76 nodes and 193 edges, the nodes representing proteins, small molecules, stimuli, and phenotypes, and the edges depicting the directed interactions between the nodes (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the structure of the prior knowledge network created in the study.

claim: Ba/F3 cells expressing FLT3ITD-TKD have significantly decreased sensitivity to TKIs compared with FLT3ITD-JMD cells.
source: As previously demonstrated, cells expressing FLT3ITD-TKD ('resistant model') have significantly decreased sensitivity to TKIs, including the recently registered FLT3-TKI Midostaurin, compared with FLT3ITD-JMD cells ('sensitive model') (Massacci et al., 2023; Pugliese et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as previously demonstrated and supported by citations.

claim: The biological replicates in the multiparametric analysis displayed Pearson correlation coefficients ranging between 0.75 and 1.
source: Briefly, the biological replicates displayed Pearson correlation coefficients ranging between 0.75 and 1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about the reproducibility of the experimental data, with reference to a figure.

claim: Principal component analysis showed that the activity level of sentinel proteins stratified cells according to both FLT3 activation status and cytokine stimulation.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) (Figure 2D) and unsupervised hierarchical clustering (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D) showed that the activity level of sentinel proteins stratified cells according to both FLT3 activation status (component 1: presence vs absence of FLT3i) and cytokine stimulation (component 2: IGF1 vs TNFα).
evidence: This is a statement about the results of PCA analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Among all the kinase inhibitor-treated conditions, only the JNKi treatment groups with the FLT3i treated samples in both cell lines.
source: Of note, among all the KINi-treated conditions, only the JNKi treatment groups with the FLT3i treated samples in both cell lines.
evidence: This is an observation from the PCA analysis described in the text.

claim: The activation profile of 14 sentinel proteins was not able to distinguish cells according to the distinct FLT3-ITD insertion sites.
source: On the contrary, the activation profile of these 14 sentinel proteins was not able to distinguish cells according to the distinct FLT3-ITD insertion sites (circles = FLT3ITD-JMD and squares = FLT3ITD-TKD) (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a statement about the results of the analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: Two FLT3-ITD-specific PKNs were obtained, accounting for 206 and 208 nodes and 756 and 782 edges, for FLT3ITD-JMD and FLT3ITD-TKD, respectively.
source: Using this strategy, we obtained two FLT3-ITD-specific PKNs, accounting for 206 and 208 nodes and 756 and 782 edges, for FLT3ITD-JMD and FLT3ITD-TKD, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about the structure of the optimized networks.

claim: The fit between simulated and experimental data was generally higher in the FLT3ITD-JMD model than in the FLT3ITD-TKD model.
source: As shown in Figure 3A, panel 3, the fit between simulated and experimental data was generally higher in the FLT3ITD-JMD model, which has been more extensively characterized by the scientific community than the FLT3ITD-TKD system.
evidence: This is a statement about the quality of the model fit with reference to a figure.

claim: The two Boolean models display a different structure, with most of the interactions being cell-specific.
source: Interestingly, the two Boolean models display a different structure, and most of the interactions are cell-specific (blue edges), with only a few edges shared among the two networks (e.g. TNFR-FLT3, STAT3-STAT5A, p70S6K-p38, etc.).
evidence: This is a statement about the structural differences between the two models.

claim: The architectural differences between the models demonstrate a profound rewiring of the signal downstream of FLT3 as a result of the different locations of the ITD.
source: The architectural differences between the models demonstrate a profound rewiring of the signal downstream of FLT3 as a result of the different locations of the ITD.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural differences observed in the models.

claim: The activation status of the nodes in the two generated models is highly comparable with the level of regulatory phosphorylations reported in the reference dataset.
source: The activation status of the nodes in the two generated models is highly comparable with the level of regulatory phosphorylations reported in the reference dataset, supporting our models (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a statement about the validation of the models using independent data.

claim: FLT3ITD-JMD and FLT3ITD-TKD Boolean models were able to recapitulate the different TKI sensitivity of FLT3-ITD cells.
source: Importantly, our strategy demonstrated that FLT3ITD-JMD and FLT3ITD-TKD Boolean models were able to recapitulate the different TKI sensitivity of FLT3-ITD cells (Figure 3E, right panels) (Massacci et al., 2023; Pugliese et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a statement about the predictive capability of the models, with reference to figures and citations.

claim: In the FLT3ITD-TKD model, the combined inhibition of JNK and FLT3 exclusively restores the TKI sensitivity in silico.
source: Interestingly, in the FLT3ITD-TKD model, the combined inhibition of JNK and FLT3, exclusively, in silico restores the TKI sensitivity, as revealed by the evaluation of the apoptosis and proliferation levels (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is a statement about the results of in silico simulations with reference to figures.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of JNK alone or in combination with Midostaurin significantly increased the percentage of apoptotic FLT3ITD-TKD cells.
source: Our data indicate that JNK plays a crucial role in cell survival of FLT3-ITD cells, since its pharmacological inhibition (SP600125) alone or in combination with Midostaurin (PKC412) significantly increased the percentage of apoptotic FLT3ITD-TKD cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental results with reference to a figure.

claim: The apoptosis of FLT3ITD-TKD patient-derived blasts is increased upon pharmacological inhibition of JNK.
source: Remarkably, the apoptosis of FLT3ITD-TKD patients-derived blasts is increased upon pharmacological inhibition of JNK (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental results with patient samples, with reference to a figure.

claim: A significant reduction of proliferating FLT3ITD-TKD cells was observed upon combined treatment with JNK inhibitor and Midostaurin versus Midostaurin alone.
source: Consistently, in these experimental conditions, we observed a significant reduction of proliferating FLT3ITD-TKD cells versus cells treated with Midostaurin alone (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental results with reference to a figure.

claim: Pharmacological suppression of ERK1/2 or p38 kinases have no impact on the TKI sensitivity of FLT3ITD-TKD cells.
source: Additionally, in agreement with the models' predictions, we demonstrated that pharmacological suppression of ERK1/2 or p38 kinases have no impact on the TKI sensitivity of FLT3ITD-TKD cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental results with reference to figures.

claim: In FLT3ITD-JMD cells, Midostaurin treatment increases the dephosphorylated, cytosolic, and monomeric pool of CDK1 and inactivates CDK2.
source: In line with our previous findings (Massacci et al., 2023; Pugliese et al., 2023), in FLT3ITD-JMD cells, Midostaurin treatment increases the dephosphorylated, cytosolic, and monomeric pool of CDK1 and inactivates CDK2 (Figure 4G), leading to cell accumulation in the G1 phase (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental results with reference to figures and citations.

claim: Combined treatment of SP600125 and Midostaurin increases CDK1 and CDK2 phosphorylation and CyclinB1 levels in FLT3ITD-JMD cells.
source: Combined treatment of SP600125 and Midostaurin increases CDK1 and CDK2 phosphorylation and CyclinB1 levels, increasing the percentage of G2-M and S-phases cells, compared with Midostaurin treatment alone (Figure 4G and H).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental results with reference to figures.

claim: In FLT3ITD-TKD cells, Midostaurin treatment triggers the formation of the inactive stockpiled pre-M-phase promoting factor constituted by the CDK1-CyclinB1 complex.
source: As expected, in cells expressing FLT3ITD-TKD, Midostaurin treatment triggers the formation of the inactive stockpiled pre-M-phase promoting factor (Massacci et al., 2023), constituted by the CDK1-CyclinB1 complex (Figure 4G and I).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental results with reference to figures and a citation.

claim: Combined treatment of SP600125 and Midostaurin induces dephosphorylation of CDK1 on the inhibitory Tyr15 in FLT3ITD-TKD cells.
source: On the other hand, combined treatment of SP600125 and Midostaurin induces dephosphorylation of CDK1 on the inhibitory Tyr15 and a mild accumulation of FLT3ITD-TKD cells in G2-M phase (Figure 4G and I; Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental results with reference to figures.

claim: The combination of JNK inhibition with Midostaurin treatment impacts the cell cycle progression in TKI-resistant FLT3ITD-TKD cells, impairing their survival and reactivating the TKI-induced apoptosis.
source: These observations support the hypothesis that the combination of JNK inhibition with Midostaurin treatment impacts the cell cycle progression in TKI-resistant FLT3ITD-TKD cells, impairing their survival and reactivating the TKI-induced apoptosis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results presented.

claim: The patient cohort consisted of eight patients with FLT3ITD-JMD, four with FLT3ITD-JMD+TKD, and two with FLT3ITD-TKD.
source: Briefly, the classification of these 10 patients according to their ITD localization (see Materials and methods) was as follows: eight patients with FLT3ITD-JMD, four with FLT3ITD-JMD+TKD, and two with FLT3ITD-TKD (Figure 5A, panel b).
evidence: This is a statement about the composition of the patient cohort analyzed.

claim: Mutation profiling analysis of the patient cohort revealed a heterogeneity in the genetic background among patients and a high number of co-occurring genetic alterations.
source: Mutation profiling analysis of the patient cohort revealed a heterogeneity in the genetic background among patients and a high number of co-occurring genetic alterations (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B; Supplementary file 9).
evidence: This is a statement about the results of mutation profiling analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Patients' unsupervised hierarchical clustering according to the mutational profile or gene expression was unable to stratify patients based on their FLT3-ITD subtypes.
source: Significantly, patients' unsupervised hierarchical clustering according to the mutational profile or according to the z-score distribution of the gene expression and PCA of the gene expression data was unable to stratify patients based on their FLT3-ITD subtypes (Figure 5C and D; Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a statement about the results of clustering analysis with reference to figures.

claim: The anti-proliferative and pro-apoptotic response to FLT3 inhibition of JMD1, JMD2, JMD3, JMD7, and JMD6 models was confirmed by follow-up clinical data that displayed a favorable outcome upon treatment.
source: The anti-proliferative and pro-apoptotic response to FLT3 inhibition (Figure 5E) of JMD1, JMD2, JMD3, JMD7, and JMD6 models was confirmed by follow-up clinical data that displayed a favorable outcome upon treatment (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a statement about the validation of model predictions with clinical data, with reference to figures.

claim: Simulations of JMD5, JMD_TKD2, JMD_TKD3, and TKD1 models showed an opposite outcome with respect to real-life clinical observations.
source: Conversely, simulations of JMD5, JMD_TKD2, JMD_TKD3, and TKD1 models showed an opposite outcome with respect to real-life clinical observations (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a statement about the discrepancy between model predictions and clinical data, with reference to a figure.

claim: JNK inhibition appeared to be a promising approach to alleviate the resistant phenotype of the clinically-not-responder TKD2 patient.
source: Interestingly and in line with our previous cell-line-based findings, JNK inhibition appeared to be a promising approach to alleviate the resistant phenotype of the clinically-not-responder TKD2 (Figure 5B), as revealed by the diminished levels of 'apoptosis inhibition' and 'proliferation' (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This is a statement about the model prediction for a specific patient, with reference to figures.

claim: The model suggests that the effect of combinatorial FLT3i and JNKi treatment increases AML cell death through the STAT3/STAT5A axis in the TKD2 patient.
source: Our model suggests that the effect of combinatorial FLT3i and JNKi treatment increases AML cell death through the STAT3/STA5A axis (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanistic prediction from the model, with reference to a figure.

claim: Boolean logic models are crucial in guiding experimental approaches for discovering rational drug combinations.
source: Computational approaches that can predict drug synergy, including Boolean logic models, are crucial in guiding experimental approaches for discovering rational drug combinations.
evidence: This is stated as a general principle in the Introduction.

claim: In the Boolean model, a biological process or pathway of interest is modeled in the form of a signed and direct graphic with edges representing the regulatory relationship between the nodes.
source: In the Boolean model, a biological process or pathway of interest is modeled in the form of a signed and direct graphic with edges representing the regulatory relationship (activating or inhibitory) between the nodes (proteins).
evidence: This is a description of the Boolean modeling approach used in the study.

claim: Logical operators (AND, OR, and NOT) are employed to dynamically describe how the signal is integrated and propagated in the system over time to reach a terminal state.
source: Logical operators (AND, OR, and NOT) are then employed to dynamically describe how the signal is integrated and propagated in the system over time to reach a terminal state.
evidence: This is a description of the Boolean modeling approach.

claim: Once optimized, Boolean models offer the ability to test for the effect of perturbation of the nodes on the resulting phenotype.
source: Once optimized, these models offer the ability to test for the effect of perturbation of the nodes on the resulting phenotype (e.g. in silico knock-out), allowing us to generate novel hypotheses and to predict the efficacy of novel drug combinations (Hemedan et al., 2022; Le Novère, 2015; Montagud et al., 2022; Schwab et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of Boolean models, supported by citations.

claim: CellNOptR was used to implement an integrated strategy that combines prior knowledge signaling networks with multiparametric analysis and Boolean logic modeling.
source: Among the different computational methods available, in the present study, we utilized CellNOptR (Terfve et al., 2012) to implement an integrated strategy that combines prior knowledge signaling networks (PKNs) with multiparametric analysis and Boolean logic modeling.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodology used in the study, with a citation.

claim: Midostaurin is a recently FDA-approved multi-kinase inhibitor.
source: We and others have demonstrated that the location (insertion site) of the ITD is a crucial prognostic factor: treatment with the recently FDA-approved multi-kinase inhibitor Midostaurin and standard frontline chemotherapy has a significant beneficial effect only in patients carrying the ITDs in the JMD domain, whereas no beneficial effect has been shown in patients carrying ITDs in the TKD region (Rücker et al., 2022; Pugliese et al., 2023; Massacci et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the drug Midostaurin.

claim: The experimental model consisted of hematopoietic Ba/F3 cells stably expressing the FLT3 gene with ITDs insertions in the JMD domain (aa 598) or in the TKD1 (aa 613) region.
source: Our experimental model consisted of hematopoietic Ba/F3 cells stably expressing the FLT3 gene with ITDs insertions in the JMD domain (aa 598) or in the TKD1 (aa 613) region (henceforth 'FLT3ITD-JMD' and 'FLT3ITD-TKD' cells, respectively).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental model used in the study.

claim: SIGNOR is a public repository that captures more than 35K causal interactions among biological entities.
source: Briefly, SIGNOR is a public repository that captures more than 35K causal interactions (up/down-regulations) among biological entities and represents them in the form of a direct and signed network (Lo Surdo et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a description of the SIGNOR database, with a citation.

claim: Little is known about the specific signaling pathways downstream of the non-canonical FLT3ITD-TKD.
source: As little is known about the specific signaling pathways downstream of the non-canonical FLT3ITD-TKD, we enriched the pre-PKN, deriving new edges from cell-specific experimental data of both FLT3ITD-TKD and FLT3ITD-JMD expressing cell lines (see Materials and methods, Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as a motivation for enriching the PKN with experimental data.

claim: MAPKs, PI3K-AKT-mTOR, and STATs are the main pathways downstream of FLT3, IGF1R, and TNFR.
source: Generally, MAPKs, PI3K-AKT-mTOR, and STATs are the main pathways downstream of FLT3, IGF1R, and TNFR; we selected six key kinases in the FLT3-ITD PKN, and we perturbed their activity with small molecule inhibitors in presence or in absence of the FLT3i Midostaurin.
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge about signaling pathways.

claim: The observed modulation of the readouts was consistent with the experimental evidence reported in the literature.
source: Overall, the observed modulation of the readouts was consistent with the experimental evidence reported in the literature (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C, black squares in the heatmap).
evidence: This is a statement about the validation of the experimental results with literature, with reference to a figure.

claim: The unsupervised hierarchical clustering of the 14 analytes revealed different groups according to the pathway proximity of the nodes or according to their regulatory role.
source: Interestingly, the unsupervised hierarchical clustering of the 14 analytes revealed different groups according to the pathway proximity of the nodes (e.g. JNK-p38; p70S6K-RPS6; STAT3-STAT5) or according to their regulatory role (e.g. GSK3a/b, PTEN and TSC2, acting as negative regulators, cluster together) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a statement about the results of clustering analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: The characterization of the genotype-dependent rewiring of signaling pathways cannot be obtained by simply looking at single proteins in the multiparametric dataset, but rather requires a modeling approach.
source: Together, these observations suggest that the characterization of the genotype-dependent rewiring of signaling pathways cannot be obtained by simply looking at single proteins in our multiparametric dataset, but rather requires a modeling approach.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results and a justification for the modeling approach.

claim: The variation in the node count between the two PKNs results from the inclusion of a different number of AND Boolean operators during the expansion step.
source: The variation in the node count between these two PKNs results from the inclusion of a different number of AND Boolean operators during the expansion step, while the difference in edge numbers is primarily due to different variations in the data, leading to distinct edge connections in the imputation step.
evidence: This is an explanation of the differences between the two PKNs.

claim: The difference in edge numbers between the two PKNs is primarily due to different variations in the data, leading to distinct edge connections in the imputation step.
source: The variation in the node count between these two PKNs results from the inclusion of a different number of AND Boolean operators during the expansion step, while the difference in edge numbers is primarily due to different variations in the data, leading to distinct edge connections in the imputation step.
evidence: This is an explanation of the differences between the two PKNs.

claim: The FLT3ITD-JMD model has been more extensively characterized by the scientific community than the FLT3ITD-TKD system.
source: As shown in Figure 3A, panel 3, the fit between simulated and experimental data was generally higher in the FLT3ITD-JMD model, which has been more extensively characterized by the scientific community than the FLT3ITD-TKD system.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the better fit of the FLT3ITD-JMD model.

claim: JNK has already been shown to play a role in cell cycle regulation through the inactivation of CDC25C, a phosphatase and positive regulator of CDK1.
source: Interestingly, JNK has already been shown to play a role in cell cycle regulation through the inactivation of CDC25C, a phosphatase and positive regulator of CDK1 (Gutierrez et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: The cell cycle controls the FLT3ITD-TKD TKI resistance via the WEE1-CDK1 axis.
source: Recently, we revealed that the cell cycle controls the FLT3ITD-TKD TKI resistance via the WEE1-CDK1 axis (Massacci et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work by the authors, with a citation.

claim: Follow-up clinical data were available for 10 out of 14 patients.
source: Follow-up clinical data were available for 10 out of 14 patients (Figure 5B, Supplementary file 9).
evidence: This is a statement about the availability of clinical data.

claim: The more complex mutational landscape of the TKD1 patient cannot be recapitulated by the scaffold model.
source: One possible explanation is that the more complex mutational landscape of the TKD1 patient cannot be recapitulated by our scaffold model (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated as a possible explanation for the discrepancy between model predictions and clinical data.

claim: The two trained Boolean logic models have predictive power and can contribute to identifying potential therapeutic strategies improving clinical outcome of FLT3ITD-TKD patients.
source: Overall, this analysis showcases the two trained Boolean logic models have predictive power and can contribute to identifying potential therapeutic strategies improving clinical outcome of FLT3ITD-TKD patients.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of patient-specific models.

claim: Cancer is primarily a signaling disease in which gene mutations and epigenetic alterations drastically impact crucial tumor pathways, leading to aberrant survival and cell proliferation.
source: Cancer is primarily a signaling disease in which gene mutations and epigenetic alterations drastically impact crucial tumor pathways, leading to aberrant survival and cell proliferation.
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge about cancer in the Discussion.

claim: Nearly all molecularly targeted therapeutic drugs are directed against signaling molecules.
source: Indeed, nearly all molecularly targeted therapeutic drugs are directed against signaling molecules (Min and Lee, 2022).
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge with a citation.

claim: The success of targeted therapies is often limited, and drug resistance mechanisms arise, leading to therapy failure and dismal patient prognosis.
source: However, the success of targeted therapies is often limited, and drug resistance mechanisms arise, leading to therapy failure and dismal patient prognosis.
evidence: This is stated as a general problem in cancer therapy.

claim: A comprehensive, patient-specific characterization of signaling network rewiring can offer an unprecedented opportunity to identify novel promising, personalized combinatorial treatments.
source: To address this issue, a comprehensive, patient-specific characterization of signaling network rewiring can offer an unprecedented opportunity to identify novel promising, personalized combinatorial treatments.
evidence: This is stated as a motivation for the study.

claim: Logic-based models have already been proven to successfully meet the challenge of identifying drug combinations, thanks to their ability to condense the signaling features of a system and to infer the response triggered by genetic and chemical perturbations to the system in silico.
source: Logic-based models have already been proven to successfully meet this challenge, thanks to their ability to condense the signaling features of a system and to infer the response triggered by genetic and chemical perturbations to the system in silico (Lee et al., 2012; Montagud et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The approach involved building a model representing the patient-specific cell state or disease status and inferring novel combinatorial anti-cancer treatments that may overcome drug resistance.
source: Our approach involved building a model representing the patient-specific cell state or disease status and inferring novel combinatorial anti-cancer treatments that may overcome drug resistance.
evidence: This is a description of the approach used in the study.

claim: The group recently showed that the location of the ITD insertion affects the sensitivity to TKIs therapy through a WEE1-CDK1-dependent mechanism.
source: Our group recently showed, by integrating unbiased mass spectrometry-based phosphoproteomics with literature-derived signaling networks, that the location of the ITD insertion affects the sensitivity to TKIs therapy through a WEE1-CDK1-dependent mechanism.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work by the authors.

claim: The work enabled obtaining a nearly complete, though static, picture of how FLT3-ITD mutations rewire signaling networks.
source: Our work enabled us to obtain a nearly complete, though static, picture of how FLT3-ITD mutations rewire signaling networks.
evidence: This is stated as a result of previous work by the authors.

claim: The main goal of the present study was the generation of clinically relevant, predictive models of the FLT3-ITD-dependent cell state.
source: The main goal of the present study was the generation of clinically relevant, predictive models of the FLT3-ITD-dependent cell state.
evidence: This is stated as the main goal of the study.

claim: The study aims to use the models to predict in silico the TKI sensitivity upon multiple simultaneous perturbations.
source: We aim to use these models to predict in silico the TKI sensitivity upon multiple simultaneous perturbations (i); to generate personalized models by combining patient-specific genomic and transcriptomic datasets (ii); and to propose novel, effective, patient-specific anti-cancer treatments (iii).
evidence: This is stated as one of the aims of the study.

claim: The study aims to generate personalized models by combining patient-specific genomic and transcriptomic datasets.
source: We aim to use these models to predict in silico the TKI sensitivity upon multiple simultaneous perturbations (i); to generate personalized models by combining patient-specific genomic and transcriptomic datasets (ii); and to propose novel, effective, patient-specific anti-cancer treatments (iii).
evidence: This is stated as one of the aims of the study.

claim: The study aims to propose novel, effective, patient-specific anti-cancer treatments.
source: We aim to use these models to predict in silico the TKI sensitivity upon multiple simultaneous perturbations (i); to generate personalized models by combining patient-specific genomic and transcriptomic datasets (ii); and to propose novel, effective, patient-specific anti-cancer treatments (iii).
evidence: This is stated as one of the aims of the study.

claim: Cell Network Optimizer software was previously developed.
source: By taking advantage of the previously developed Cell Network Optimizer software (Terfve et al., 2012), we employed a multi-step strategy that trains a PKN with a large-scale multiparametric dataset by using a Boolean logic modeling formalism.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the software used, with a citation.

claim: Manually curated data were made publicly available and can be freely explored by using tools offered by the SIGNOR resource website or downloaded for local analysis, in compliance with the FAIR principles.
source: Manually curated data were made publicly available and can be freely explored by using tools offered by the SIGNOR resource website or downloaded for local analysis, in compliance with the FAIR principles (Wilkinson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about data availability, with a citation to the FAIR principles.

claim: The xMAP technology was used to interrogate signaling in FLT3-ITD cells treated with a panel of nine different perturbations.
source: Second, we used the xMAP technology to interrogate signaling in FLT3-ITD cells treated with a panel of nine different perturbations.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methodology used.

claim: Analysis of the large multiplex signaling dataset revealed a clear separation between TKI-treated and untreated cells as well as IGF1 and TNFα-stimulated cells.
source: Analysis of this large multiplex signaling dataset, consisting of 16 distinct experimental conditions, revealed a clear separation between TKI-treated and untreated cells as well as IGF1 and TNFα-stimulated cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of the analysis.

claim: There was no clear separation between FLT3ITD-JMD and FLT3ITD-TKD cells upon clustering based on signaling parameters.
